text:
maya: Quick heads-up — noticed a regression in multi-node 8xA100 pipeline runs. p50 token latency jumped ~30% after the kernel-selection change we rolled yesterday. Suspect NCCL algo/proto choices interacting badly with our micro-batch sizes.
samir: ugh. do you have nccl-tests or perf traces?
maya: pasted a short nccl-tests run from the repro instance (node pair). numbers are single-shot all-reduce for 16MB chunks: 
```
Allreduce 16MB: 1) NCCL_ALGO=RING NCCL_PROTO=LL => 52 GB/s
Allreduce 16MB: 2) NCCL_ALGO=RING NCCL_PROTO=LL128 => 68 GB/s
Allreduce 16MB: 3) NCCL_ALGO=TREE NCCL_PROTO=LL => 45 GB/s
Allreduce 16MB: 4) NCCL_ALGO=TREE NCCL_PROTO=LL128 => 50 GB/s
```
maya: but when we run the real model workload the end-to-end tokens/sec is worse with LL128 in a few cases — likely because fragmentation + more small all-reduces (KV cache flush) kills overlap.
jin: can you share the perfviz flame? curious about comm vs compute overlap.
maya: attaching quick snapshot (link) — but here's the inline summary: main stage shows frequent ~1.5ms all-reduces every micro-batch, but compute gaps are ~2ms so overlap is marginal. with LL128 the internal per-transfer size drops causing overhead.
ryan: did we change channel count? remember we recently lowered NCCL_NCHANNELS to 1 for stability on older interconnects. that could reduce parallelism for LL128.
maya: good point — current repro used NCCL_NCHANNELS=1. when I flip to 4 on the same job, raw nccl-tests throughput for LL128 increases to ~90 GB/s for that 16MB size, and E2E token latency improves ~12%.
samir: nice — so combo of proto + channel count matters. what's the default we ship in Private deployments? we need a safe fallback.
jin: also check NCCL_ALGO and bucket sizing in our collective implementation. smaller buckets => more frequent collectives. KV cache eviction pattern in long-context workloads can cause sudden bursts of tiny all-reduces. we should add jittered flushing / coalescing.
ryan: action items: 1) repro matrix for {ALGO in [RING,TREE], PROTO in [LL,LL128], NCHANNELS in [1,2,4,8]} with our micro-batch distribution; 2) run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to capture algo selection in logs; 3) add a latency histogram for all-reduce calls to perf traces.
maya: started a job scheduler run with that matrix on the lab cluster (job id 2026-117). I'll drop logs here as they complete.
ops-bot: Job 2026-117 queued on cluster lab-west-2 (8 nodes). ETA ~25m.
samir: one more thing — check NIC tuning: SQP vs SQ? (sorry mixer of names). ensure socket ifname pinned, and confirm we haven't regressed TCP fallback. small collective shapes are very sensitive to ppn and NIC config.
jin: also try NCCL_TOPO_FILE if you can capture the topology. often tree algo is better when you have multiple NVLinks inside a node and a single IB link across nodes.
maya: noted. I've appended current envs in the run: 
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
NCCL_ALGO=RING
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
NCCL_NCHANNELS=4
NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=ib0
```
maya: early results: RING+LL128+4ch wins on throughput microbench, but E2E wins only when we coalesce KV cache flushes to >8MB per collective. otherwise many tiny all-reduces dominate.
ryan: sounds like two levers: runtime should keep proto=LL128 by default for large transfers but fall back to LL for tiny transfers or auto-adjust channel count. also runtime could batch KV invalidations across steps.
samir: agree. can we expose a knob in the deployment config for "comm_profile" with presets (low_latency, high_throughput, conservative)? that would help Dedicated customers.
jin: and add a safety check: if avg collective size < 256KB then force PROTO=LL and reduce channels. LL128 overhead for small sizes is real.
maya: I'll open a PR with a minimal heuristic: if median_collective_size < 1MB -> PROTO=LL, NCHANNELS=1; else PROTO=LL128, NCHANNELS=4. will run A/B against canary tomorrow.
samir: please include change log and perf numbers in PR. we'll need an opt-out for users that want aggressive LL128 even on small sizes.
maya: ack. assigning to me. ping me if you want to reproduce: job 2026-117 will keep logs in /var/logs/perf/2026-117.tar.gz when done.
ops-bot: Job 2026-117 completed. artifacts available at s3://redwood-perf/lab-west-2/2026-117/
ryan: thanks — once we confirm, let's schedule a short sync with Infra to validate NIC settings before promoting to canary. :eyes:
samir: cool. also add a short note in the release notes about potential latency tradeoffs when kernel-selection heuristics change. we've got one spike already.
maya: will do. closing the loop after PR lands and we run the canary. :white_check_mark:
